item.aggregated_output:
# Tensile test elastic modulus estimates

For each material, an ordinary least-squares line with a freely fitted intercept was fit to all measured stress-strain points pooled across its specimens. The slope is reported as the elastic modulus. Fits use the full measured strain range (0.0002–0.0020); no specimen-level averaging or interval selection was applied.

| Material | Specimens | Points | Modulus (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| aluminum | 3 | 30 | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.99834 |
| steel | 3 | 30 | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.99844 |
| titanium | 3 | 30 | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.99788 |

item.text:
Analyzed the 90 measurements with pooled ordinary least-squares linear fits, including a fitted intercept, across the full strain range. The estimated moduli are:

- **Aluminum:** 69.38 GPa (R² = 0.99834)
- **Steel:** 199.06 GPa (R² = 0.99844)
- **Titanium:** 116.56 GPa (R² = 0.99788)

The plot is [stress_strain_fits.png](/private/tmp/tmpttoxbepb/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/stress_strain_fits.png), and the short write-up is [results.md](/private/tmp/tmpttoxbepb/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.md). I also added [results.csv](/private/tmp/tmpttoxbepb/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.csv) with the fit details.

Calkit now records the analysis as a pipeline stage in [calkit.yaml](/private/tmp/tmpttoxbepb/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/calkit.yaml). The pipeline ran successfully and is up to date.
